suggestions.quote: By the last square, the board owes more wheat than the whole world grows in over a thousand years (c11).
suggestions.fix: Across all sixty-four squares, the board owes more wheat than the whole world grows in over a thousand years (c11).

suggestions.quote: One grain on the first square, and double on every square after (c05).
suggestions.fix: One grain on the first square, doubled on every square to over eighteen quintillion grains (c05).

keep.quote: Never hit zero, and by day two hundred and sixty-seven your account holds more cents than the estimated number of hydrogen atoms in the observable universe (c12).
This has happened before. For real. In 1324, a king from Mali, Mansa Musa, gave away so much gold in Cairo that gold stayed cheap there for at least twelve years (c06).
Right here in Berlin, by late 1923, a loaf of bread cost about two hundred billion marks (c01). Anna's board is heading the same way.
